correctness.rationale: Dihedral averaging is feasible and does not increase the nonconstant operator norm. In Fourier cosine coordinate x the drop is aU(x)+bV(x), with U=2(1−x) and V=4(1−x²). On a=qb the endpoints c and −1 have the same drop bE, and strict concavity gives the minimum there. The quadratic vertex is −q/4. For 4|n it lies strictly to the right of the midpoint of −sin(2π/n) and 0 since 1−cos(2π/n)<sin(2π/n); the positive nodes are farther from the vertex, so 0 is nearest. For n≡2 mod 4 the vertex is −s², strictly between −s and 0, with −s and +s the two grid nodes bracketing it, so −s is nearest. Both arguments include the smallest size in their regime. The upper and lower sampled drops therefore balance at b=2/(M+E). The proposed holding is strictly positive by the two residue-class formulas. For arbitrary orbit probabilities, the constraint vector (U(d),V(d)) is a strictly positive combination of the vectors at c and −1: the coefficient at c is V(d)/V(c), and the other coefficient is positive because U(x)/V(x)=1/[2(1+x)] increases as x decreases. Their sum is M/E by evaluation at (q,1). It follows that (M/E)(1−μ)≤1+μ, with equality forcing the two independent endpoint constraints and hence invariant uniqueness. Direct substitution and s∼π/n prove the holding law and all limits. Full-matrix uniqueness is not implied.
residual_risks: No claim about nonreversible chains, finite-time total variation or uniqueness among spatially varying optimizers.
